```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

HowMaHiCo turns LC-immunopeptidomics search-engine output into self-contained
interactive HTML QC reports. It reads FragPipe, DIA-NN and PEAKS exports (and,
through a YAML dictionary, most other tabular formats), normalises them into one
long-format table called `pep_all`, and renders parameterised report templates
against it.

This article walks through a complete analysis. Everything here is also
available as a **runnable script**:

```{r get-script, eval = FALSE}
HowMaHiCo::get_pipeline_script("howmahico_pipeline.R")
```

That script starts in demo mode, so sourcing it as-is runs the whole pipeline on
a small simulated dataset shipped with the package — useful for checking an
install before pointing it at real data.

## Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("DavidGZ1/HowMaHiCo")

# Optional: the advanced-quantification report (06) uses limma when available
BiocManager::install("limma")
```

Rendering reports needs pandoc, which RStudio bundles; outside RStudio, install
it separately. Without limma, report 06 still runs and falls back to a Welch
t-test.

## The shape of a run

```
search output (psm.tsv / report.tsv / peptide.csv)
   |  read + parse + annotate
   v
pep_all  ->  cached as <Subset>_pep_all.rda
   |  render
   v
HTML reports  +  csv/xlsx tables  +  optional png figures
```

Two things drive everything: the **annotation table**, which says which files
belong to which experimental group, and the **`Software`** parameter, which
selects the loader.

## 1. The annotation table

Generate a skeleton with one row per data file, then fill in the experimental
columns by hand:

```{r annot-generate, eval = FALSE}
library(HowMaHiCo)

get_annot_fragpipe(dir_data = "2_data") |>            # or get_annot_diann() / get_annot_peaks()
  write.csv(row.names = FALSE, file = "1_documentation/sample_annotation.csv")
```

Open the csv and complete `Condition`, `BioReplicate`, `TechReplicate` and
`Sample_ID`. Two behaviours are worth knowing, because both are easy to trip
over:

- **Inclusion** — only samples listed in the table are read and reported. A
  sample sitting in the data folder but missing from the table is silently
  excluded, so the table is also how you subset a run.
- **Ordering** — Conditions, replicates and samples appear in every plot and
  table in the **row order of the csv**. Order the rows the way you want them
  displayed.

`Sample_ID` can also be filled from a Bruker HyStar sample list with
`get_annot_sampleid()`.

Here is the completed annotation table that ships with the simulated dataset:

```{r annot-demo}
library(HowMaHiCo)

annot <- read_annot(system.file("extdata", "sim_fragpipe_dda_annotation.csv",
                                package = "HowMaHiCo"))
annot
```

## 2. Parse once into `pep_all`

`build_pep_all()` runs the loader and writes a cache. Each focused report then
renders against that cache, so the raw files are parsed once rather than once
per report.

```{r build}
sim_dir <- system.file("extdata", "sim_fragpipe_dda", package = "HowMaHiCo")

pep_all <- build_pep_all(
  software       = "fragpipe_dda_individual",
  folder_data    = sim_dir,
  annotation     = annot,
  shortpep_range = mhc_length_window("MHC1")   # 8-13 AA for human HLA-I
)

dim(pep_all)
```

One row per peptide-sample observation:

```{r peek}
pep_all[1:5, c("Sample", "Condition", "Peptide", "Length", "Charge", "Area")]
```

`mhc_length_window()` is the single source of truth for the ligand-length
window — `"MHC1"` (8–13), `"MHC1_mouse"` (7–11, murine H-2 runs shorter) or
`"MHC2"` (12–25). The subset of `pep_all` inside that window is what the reports
call *selected peptides*.

```{r windows}
rbind(MHC1 = mhc_length_window("MHC1"),
      MHC1_mouse = mhc_length_window("MHC1_mouse"),
      MHC2 = mhc_length_window("MHC2"))
```

## 3. Render reports

`run_howmahico_report()` wraps `rmarkdown::render()`: it locates the template
inside the installed package and knits it in a clean environment. One call
renders one report.

```{r render, eval = FALSE}
report_params <- list(
  SampleSet     = "my_experiment",
  Provider      = "My Lab",          # "" prints a generic attribution
  Subset        = "dda_all",
  FolderData    = "2_data",
  FolderResults = "3_results",
  FolderFigures = "4_figures",
  Software      = "fragpipe_dda_combined",
  MHCclass      = "MHC1"
)

run_howmahico_report("01_id_counts",
                     params = c(report_params, list(PepAllSource = "cached")),
                     output_file = "01_id_counts.html")
```

The templates on offer:

| Template | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| `00_mhc_report` | All-in-one QC report; parses the raw files itself |
| `00_mhc_upsets` | Overlap / UpSet plots only |
| `01_id_counts` | ID counts, length and charge distributions, motifs, PTM profile |
| `02_overlaps` | Replicate, cross-condition and pairwise overlap |
| `03_lcms_qc` | RT / ion mobility / *m/z* distributions, Score and mass-error QC |
| `04_quant` | log2(Area) correlation between samples, Area %CV |
| `05_quality_score` | Per-sample immunopeptidomics quality score |
| `06_quant_stats` | Differential abundance between Conditions |
| `07_pepchem` | Amino-acid composition, positional motifs, GRAVY and other descriptors |
| `08_prot_all` | Source proteins: ligands per protein, and engine-reported protein values |

Each focused report gets `pep_all` via its `PepAllSource` parameter:
`"cached"` (the default — load `<Subset>_pep_all.rda`), `"rda"` (load an explicit
`PepAllFile`), or `"build"` (parse the raw output itself, skipping step 2
entirely).

## 4. Output

Written to `<FolderResults>/<Subset>/` on every run:

- `<Subset>_pep_all.csv` — the unified peptide table
- `<Subset>_counts_pep_all_condition.csv` — identification counts per Condition
- `<Subset>_seq_by_condition.xlsx` — sequences per Condition
- `<Subset>_<report>_input_params.csv` — every parameter used, for reproducibility

`CsvSave = TRUE` adds the intermediate tables; `PlotsSave = TRUE` writes every
figure as png to `<FolderFigures>/<Subset>/`. The HTML report goes to
`output_file`.

## A tool with no built-in loader

For a tabular export HowMaHiCo does not know, describe it in a YAML dictionary
instead of writing R code:

```{r custom, eval = FALSE}
get_dictionary_template("my_tool.yaml")     # fill in the column mapping, then:

build_pep_all("custom", folder_data = "2_data", annotation = annot,
              dictionary = "my_tool.yaml", file_rda = "2_data/pep_all.rda")
```

The dictionary maps raw column names onto the `pep_all` schema; reference
dictionaries for the three built-in engines ship in
`inst/extdata/dictionaries/`.
